page.layout: One page of running text, with notes in the left margin. Running head at the top right. Page number at the top left. Full-width title heading in the middle of the page, then a paragraph with a large initial below it. Left margin note beside the last paragraph.

main_text.p: Volucria, quod in aere volent, dicta sunt aues.
Humi gradientia vel ambulant, vt homo & quadrupedes, vel reptant vt reptilia.
Amphibia animalia dicuntur, quae an-cipitis sunt natura, inter aerea & aquea, hoc est, partim in aere, partim in aqua viuunt, vt rana, crocodilus, lutra, laxus, fiber, natrix, mer-gus, anas.

Huiusmodi sunt sanguinea, succedunt ex-sanguia, sanguinis scilicet expertia, vt sunt polypus, sepia, lolligo, crustacea item, vt cancer, locu-sta, squilla, & testacea, vt limaces terrestres, cochlea marina, ostrea, pectines, concha.
Hec est compendiosa animalium familia. Nunc opera pretium erit recensere quibus animantibus, horumq; partibus, tam externis, quam internis hominis potissimum alantur, ex-ordium sumendo ab auibus.
main_text.head: De auibus in genere, earumque differentiis in re cibaria.
main_text.p: NE nihil, quod vitae interest, omittatur, vtque lectorem pleniori atque vlteriore obsequio demereat, adnotare hic oportebit, complures in auium genere reperiri differentias, tum à tempore, ætate, victu, tum loco, cœloq;, quæ auium ipsarum car-Aues sunt animal bipes pen-natum, a-gule [?] & le-ue.

page.notes: The left margin note "a-gule" and "le-ue" are hard to read; "gule" is doubtful. The scan is slightly blurred at the lower left. Long s is written as plain s throughout, as instructed. The printed "f" in "fint", "fanguinea" and "fepia" is read as long s and given as "sunt", "sanguinea" and "sepia". The first line "Volucria" is a continuation from the previous page.
